Definition: from G4314 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join:--run (thither to, to).
BiblicalUsage: Prostrecho means to run toward, to hasten to meet. Philip ran to the Ethiopian's chariot and heard him reading Isaiah; when the people saw Jesus coming down from the mount, they were greatly amazed, and running to Him saluted Him; and a rich young ruler came running to Jesus and kneeled before Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe running to Jesus is the right hurry: Philip ran to a stranger's chariot, the crowd ran to the mount, and the young ruler ran to ask about eternal life.
